request.prompt:
VIEW 4 — THE CREATURE FROM THE END OF THE MUDFLAT, CLOSE. The same place, the same hand and the same moonlit night as the first image.

ONE single full-frame view. Not a grid, not panels, not insets. No text, no labels, no interface.

The eye stands at a player's eye height on a narrow ridge of dry black mud, three blocks wide, with still black sea water on both sides, near the south end of the mudflat, looking south. A line of wooden marker stakes with small lit lamps runs along the ridge toward a small square stone landing stage at the edge of a channel of open black sea water about sixty blocks wide. On the stage stands a small slate-roofed stone ferry house, its door shut, no boat visible anywhere. On the far shore of the channel, opposite, an identical small stone ferry house with its door shut.
Beyond the channel, filling the upper two thirds of the frame, the creature lies on its bank of mud: a whale-like leviathan built of dark grey-green, black and deepslate blocks, so large it is a hill — its head toward the viewer, a vast low mouth hanging open at the front with pale teeth like posts, above the mouth a closed eye, and above that a tall pale carved stone slab driven into the forehead; its ridged back rising behind; on its right (west) flank three dark torn wounds. Beside the ridge in the foreground, a round dark pit in the mud. The full moon over the creature, moonlight silvering the wet mud; a thin mist thinning over the black water.
request.style_note: The Stranding: every image in this series is one place drawn in the same hand — a Minecraft Java Edition build shown as a high-quality in-game screenshot with a soft night shader. Every surface is made of visible one-metre cubic blocks with vanilla Minecraft textures (cobblestone, stone bricks, spruce and dark oak planks and logs, deepslate, mud and packed mud, black and grey concrete, prismarine, lanterns, glass panes), crisp block edges, no smooth curves anywhere: round or organic forms are stepped block shapes. The place is a grey slate-roofed fishing town on cliff terraces above a bay, a plain of wet black mud risen from the bay, and a vast stranded sea creature built of dark blocks lying at the far edge of the mud. Night under a clear sky and a bright full moon: cold blue-silver moonlight on wet mud and slate roofs, deep blue-black shadows, small warm yellow pools of lantern light at doors and windows, sea water near-black with silver moon glints. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, no text, no labels, no border, no interface.
